name: mushroom pickle relish
instructions:
MUSHROOM PICKLE RELISH — the anglo-germanic lentil stew built on a PUREED-MUSHROOM GRAVY CORE (pureed mushrooms + whole lentils + tomato paste + dark bouillon + butter + flour), with DARK ALE + PICKLE JUICE + CUMIN/CARAWAY SEEDS doing the flavor injection. See [[creamy-french-lentils]] for the mustard-and-cream cousin built on the same core.

=== THE GRAVY CORE ===

- pureed portabella mushrooms (food processor or blender)
- whole lentils
- tomato paste (small, cooked hard — necessary but should NOT be tasted; the mushroom + dark ale keep it from reading red)
- dark bouillon / dark roasted vegetable broth
- butter
- flour (light roux)

=== ANGLO-GERMANIC INJECTION ===

- DARK ALE (milk stout preferred — see BITTERNESS BUDGET note)
- PICKLE JUICE (+ diced dill pickles — the sour-into-the-braise move)
- CUMIN SEEDS and/or CARAWAY SEEDS (bloomed in the butter at the start)

=== VEGETABLES ===

- ONIONS, PEAS, CARROTS, and TURNIPS.
- LEEKS are welcome too — they bridge both registers.

=== HERBS ===

- ROSEMARY. Thyme also allowed. Nothing else — fine herbs are clashing (see notes).

=== PROCEDURE (THE DARK BUILD) ===

1. SAUTÉ onions + garlic in BUTTER with the CUMIN and/or CARAWAY SEEDS blooming in the fat. (Add diced carrots/turnips here if using.)
2. PUREED MUSHROOMS: add the mushroom paste and cook it down.
3. FLOUR over the base, stir to coat.
4. DEGLAZE WITH DARK ALE (milk stout preferred). Let it reduce briefly.
5. TOMATO PASTE + DARK BROTH + WORCESTERSHIRE: the vegetarian beef-stew backbone.
6. LENTILS in; simmer until tender (turnips soften alongside).
7. TANG: PICKLE JUICE to taste, then DICED DILL PICKLES. This is the register's balancer — NOT mustard or cream (see the kit note).
8. FINISH WITH SWEET PEAS, folded in at the end.
9. Serve as a stew; or top with mash + melting cheese and bake for the cottage-pie format (see PIE FORMAT note).
notes:
=== RENAMED FROM 'MUSHROOMED LENTILS GERMAN' (2026-10-31) ===

The mushroomed-lentils taxonomy is dissolved — these were really different stews. Renamed MUSHROOM PICKLE RELISH for the dish's actual identity: the mushroom + pickle axis. The PUREED-MUSHROOM GRAVY CORE (pureed mushrooms + whole lentils + tomato paste + dark bouillon + butter + flour) is still the mechanism; the injection kit here is DARK ALE + PICKLE JUICE + CUMIN/CARAWAY SEEDS. ([[creamy-french-lentils]] injects mustard + cream + potato into the same core.)

=== THE ANGLO-GERMANIC INJECTION — ALE + PICKLE + SEED-SPICE ===

- DARK ALE: the bitter anchor. MILK STOUT preferred — regular stout's bitterness compounds; milk stout's lactose sweetness keeps the budget in balance (the Nigella milk-stout-oxtail lesson).
- PICKLE JUICE + DICED DILL PICKLES: the register's tang. This is the german sour-into-the-braise logic (Linsensuppe's canonical vinegar finish, sauerbraten thinking) — pickle juice is vinegar with the dill axis pre-bundled. NOT mustard, NOT cream — those belong to the french kit (see BALANCER KITS below).
- CUMIN AND/OR CARAWAY SEEDS: the seed-spice bloomed in the butter. Cumin is the tested default; CARAWAY is the german cousin (carvone — the same aroma family as dill seed, so it harmonizes with the pickle axis at the molecular level). Either or both; seeds only, never ground powder on top (over-spices).

=== BITTERNESS BUDGET — DARK ALE STRONGLY PREFERRED; MARMITE RISKS OVERLOAD HERE ===

The dish has one bitter-anchor slot, and in THIS version it really prefers DARK ALE. The german build is spare — onions/lentils and that's it — so there aren't many buffers, and the combination of STOCK + MARMITE + TOMATO PASTE can be a GLUTAMATE OVERLOAD even for a chili-dog-like meal. Marmite works in [[lentil-cottage-pie]] because rosemary/thyme and the potato back it up; here, ale. (And never both — stacking still overshoots the bitterness budget.)

=== BALANCER KITS ARE REGISTER-LOCKED ===

The french kit (wine/cream/mustard) and this kit (ale/pickle) don't cross. MUSTARD + MARMITE CLASH (confirmed by experiment). Mustard + ale is UNTESTED — flemish carbonnade (mustard melted into beer gravy) suggests it might coexist, so that edge stays open — but the working rule is: pick the register, use its kit.

=== VEGETABLES — ONIONS, PEAS, CARROTS, TURNIPS (LEEKS BRIDGE) ===

The register's vegetables assort automatically: onions (base), sweet PEAS (folded in at the end — confirmed), CARROTS, and TURNIPS (the root that belongs to this register — swede/rutabaga also valid in the same slot). Leeks are welcome in both versions of this pair — they bridge the registers.

=== TOMATO — NECESSARY BUT SHOULDN'T BE TASTED ===

Tomato paste is part of the shared core, but the finished stew should read DARK, not red. The PUREED MUSHROOMS + DARK ALE are the color-and-register blockers — they let the tomato do its warmth work without turning the dish tomato-y. Note this version takes MORE tomato paste than the french sibling (the bitter base fights tomato, so it takes more to hold the warmth leg) even though it looks darker. Calibrate by register, not color.

=== HERBS — ROSEMARY; FINE HERBS CLASHING; FLORALS FAIL COLD ===

The herb slot for both recipes in this pair is ROSEMARY/THYME ONLY; this version wants ROSEMARY. Fine herbs (parsley, basil, tarragon, fresh dill) are clashing. Floral dried herbs (coriander seed, herbes de provence) were tested and walked back — nice while hot, a tough sell once the dish COOLS, and this dish cools on the plate and reheats as leftovers as a matter of course.

=== PIE FORMAT (OPTIONAL) — THE COTTAGE LINEAGE ===

The recipe descends from cottage pie (via Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie — see REFERENCE below) and still takes the pie format when wanted: transfer the finished stew to a baking dish, top with mashed potatoes, bake ~20 min at 375°F, then scatter a MELTING cheese (cheddar or monterrey jack — not a hard grating cheese) and bake ~10-15 more until golden. As a stew it stands alone; the pie format is the presentation upgrade.

SERVING ALTERNATIVE — PIE, PEAS AND GRAVY: the northern-british pie-shop plate (mushy peas + gravy alongside/over) is the other format direction; this recipe currently takes its peas IN.

=== REFERENCE — VALIDATED EXPERIMENTS + JAMIE SCAFFOLD (READ-ONLY LOG) ===

The experiments that produced this recipe remain valid; condensed for reference:
- ORIGIN: reset onto Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie (root veg — leeks/carrots/swede/celeriac — + dried porcini + marmite + cumin seeds + crispy rosemary under mash; The Happy Foodie / Jamie's Veg). Cooked successfully as written. The dark build then departed: fewer vegetables, ale in, pickle tang.
- STOCK + VEGETABLES + GRAVY ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH — hearty stews need warmth (tomato paste + garlic) AND funkiness (marmite/worcestershire/ale) on top of stock.
- MARMITE CONFIRMED (second cook): bitterness/smokiness stock can't provide.
- MUSTARD + MARMITE CLASH (with the mustard+ale edge untested — carbonnade counterexample noted).
- CORIANDER: floral + bitter = double-clashing against the bitter anchor; herbes de provence's florals fail as the dish cools.
- CUMIN SEEDS ONLY, never ground cumin on top (over-spiced). Lemon juice/zest is the rescue if over-spiced (pulls it back old-world; NOT ginger — wrong register).
- DILL/PICKLE + BITTER: dill + tomato + pickle works when cumin + ale/marmite bitterness weighs it down — the refinement of the old hamburger-y hazard from the retired lentil wellington's spin-off era.
- ROOT VEGETABLES LIKE SPICE (turmeric in [[french-onion-vegetable-soup]], cumin here, cinnamon/nutmeg in [[root-vegetable-skillet]]); roots are the best vegetarian meat substitute at chunky cut.
- GERMAN CONVERGENCE: the sour-finished dark lentil stew is canonical german cooking (Linsensuppe, Swabian Linsen); the name acknowledges it.
- Anglo spice cabinet still to explore: allspice (whole berries, not ground), mace, white pepper, mustard powder, molasses, malt vinegar, sage. The broader three-register theory lives in articles/stew-registers.md (read-only reference).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[creamy-french-lentils]]: the same gravy core with the french injection (mustard + cream + potato). The contrast pair.
- [[lentil-cottage-pie]] / [[shittake-lentil-soup]]: the Jamie-scaffold cottage pie and the clean dark-stock soup.
- [[milk-stout-braised-beef]]: the meat expression of this register (oxtail/short rib + milk stout + a dill pickle in the braise).
- [[braised-turnips]]: natural side; shares the turnip register.
- [[relish]]: the standalone condiment expression of the pickle-tang axis.

=== THE ROSEMARY RULE (UNSOLVED — FROM THE OLD STEW FAMILY) ===

ROSEMARY BELONGS WHERE A DARK ANCHOR LIVES — ale/marmite (this recipe, [[lentil-cottage-pie]]) or dark stock ([[shittake-lentil-soup]]) — where it gives LIFT. In the celery + tomato forward stews ([[creamy-french-lentils]]; the retired italian mushroomed lentils) it tastes ORTHOGONAL. Competing theories: the dark anchor; 'something meaty'; or the CELERY itself — but [[chicken-pot-pie]] has celery AND rosemary happily, so no theory is clean. UNSOLVED. This recipe wants ROSEMARY.
original_chef: Mine — the dark build, descended from Jamie Oliver's Allotment Cottage Pie scaffold (Jamie Oliver's Veg, via The Happy Foodie; see REFERENCE notes) and converged toward german Linsensuppe logic.
